# GitHub Issue #52

## Title
Prompt templates, tool exclusion, and overrides from extensions

## Description
Follow-up to #51. A pi extension package such as [pit](https://github.com/cv/pit) can give pi's coding agent more than tools: **prompt templates** (`pi.prompts`), **which tools the model sees** (pit hides the built-in coding tools and shows only `typescript`), and **overrides** of tools and prompt text. This issue describes what pi-action does with each of these now, and how to support them.

Examples use a made-up repository `acme/xyz` with:

```yaml
extensions: |
  github:cv/pit#v0.35.1
```

## What pi-action does now

| Feature | In pi's CLI | In pi-action today |
|---|---|---|
| Prompt templates (`pi.prompts`, `.pi/prompts/*.md`, `~/.pi/agent/prompts`) | `/pit-reflect focus` expands `prompts/pit-reflect.md` (frontmatter `description`, `argument-hint`; body with `$ARGUMENTS`, `${ARGUMENTS:-default}`, `$1`, `${@:2}`) | **Ignored.** `loadExtensions` loads only `pi.durable` (or `pi.extensions`, for providers). `@pi /pit-reflect` goes to the model as plain text |
| Tool exclusion and hiding | pit's `pitLoadout` hides the declarations of `read`, `write`, `edit`, `bash` and other tools, so the model sees only `typescript` and the `allowedTools` from `pit.json`. The hidden tools can still be called through `tools.*` | **Not possible.** `Thread.open` installs `CodingTools` and then every extension. `root.configure()` gets only `{ model, cwd }`, so the model is always offered `read, write, edit, bash, typescript`. pit's `allowedTools` setting has no effect |
| Overrides of tools and sections | `pi.registerTool` with a built-in name replaces that tool, and `before_agent_start` can change the system prompt | **Partly works, but isn't documented or tested.** pi-durable applies the `wraps` (`wrapTool`, `wrapSection`) of every selected extension, and by default every installed extension is selected, so a pi-durable extension can already wrap `bash` or another extension's section. pi-action doesn't mention this in its docs or test it |

## Proposal

### 1. Tool exclusion and hiding (pi-durable `AgentState`)

pi-durable already has the right controls in `AgentChange` / `AgentState`:

- `tools: { remove: [...] }`: disables a tool completely (the model can't call it, and neither can other tools).
- `modelTools: { remove: [...] }`: the model isn't offered the tool, but other tools can still call it. This matches pit's "hidden but callable".

Add two inputs, which are applied with `root.configure()` on every run (each run reconfigures already, because the model can differ from the last run):

```yaml
exclude_tools: ''        # e.g. "bash": removed completely
model_tools_hidden: ''   # e.g. "read, write, edit, bash": hidden from the model, callable via pit's tools.*
```

- Accept `*` globs, as pit's `allowedTools` does (`compileToolPatterns`).
- Resolve names against the registry after the extensions are installed. If a name matches no tool, write a warning. If the resolved set would leave the model with **no** tools, fail the run.
- When an input is empty, pass `null` so a setting from an earlier run is cleared (the thread stores the agent state).
- Log the tools the model gets in the `🤖` setup line, which today lists each extension's own tools.

**Defaults that extensions declare.** A pi-durable `Extension` can't set `modelTools` itself, but it can do the same thing with a wrap: `wrapTool("read", (t) => ({ ...t, callers: ["tools"] }))` keeps `read` callable from other tools and stops offering it to the model. pit's durable entry could do this for `read`, `write`, `edit` and `bash`, using the `allowedTools` it already reads from `pit.json`. That change belongs in pit, not here. pi-action only needs to (a) document it, and (b) have the inputs above take precedence. Because `modelTools` only narrows and never widens, an input can't bring back a tool that a wrap set to `callers: ["tools"]`. Document this, or add a `model_tools_shown` input that does the reverse with a wrap installed last by pi-action.

### 2. Prompt templates

Load templates from:

1. The `pi.prompts` directories (or files) of every package in `extensions`, including packages that pi-action loads only for `pi.durable`. This is a change to `loadPackage` in `src/extensions.ts`.
2. `xyz/.pi/prompts/*.md`, **only with `trust_project: true`**. Anyone who can push a branch can change these files, and a template becomes the user's request.
3. `<agent_dir>/prompts/*.md`, when `agent_dir` is set.

When names collide, the first one in that order wins and the others get a log warning.

Expansion: when the **task** (the text after `@pi`) starts with `/<name>` and a template has that name, pi-action replaces the task with the expanded body. The rules follow pi's: remove the frontmatter, then substitute `$ARGUMENTS`/`$@`, `$1`…`$9`, `${@:N}` and `${ARGUMENTS:-default}`. This applies to the `## Task` of the first message, to `{{task}}` in `prompt_template`, to follow-ups (`**@alice** commented …:` followed by the expanded text), and to the `prompt` input for `pr_number` and direct runs. An unknown `/name` stays as it is.

- Log `▶ Request from @alice: /pit-reflect (prompt template from pit)`, and keep the original comment text in the entry's `data` so the thread shows what was typed.
- Optionally, list the templates (name and `description`) in a section, so the model can tell people what exists. Default off, because it costs tokens on every request.

### 3. Overrides

- Document that `wraps` work, and how they are ordered: `CodingTools` first, then the extensions in input order, and the last wrap wins.
- Add a test in `src/thread.test.ts` / `extensions.test.ts` with a faux extension that wraps `bash` and a pit section.
- Duplicate tool **names** across extensions are a different problem. Today pi-durable's composed map keeps the last one. To match pi's `registerTool` override, make this explicit: log `extension X replaces tool bash from coding-tools`, and don't reject the duplicate the way duplicate extension names are rejected.

## Work items

- [ ] `exclude_tools` and `model_tools_hidden` inputs (`action.yml`, `src/inputs.ts`, `Thread.open` → `root.configure`)
- [ ] Validation, warnings, and the tool list in the setup log
- [ ] Prompt templates: loading (`src/extensions.ts`, a new `src/prompts.ts`), expansion (`src/triggers.ts` / `src/context.ts`), `trust_project` gate
- [ ] Tests for wraps and tool replacement
- [ ] Docs: `docs/extensions.md` (new "Tools the model sees" and "Prompt templates" sections), `docs/prompts.md`, `docs/security.md` (templates from the project)
- [ ] Separate PR in pit: hide the coding tools in `pit/durable` with wraps, following `allowedTools`


Related: #53 (AGENTS.md) and #54 (skills) share the task-rewriting hook and the built-in context extension.

## Your Reply

pi-action posts your final response as a comment on this issue or pull request. **Do not post your reply yourself**, for example with `gh issue comment`, `gh pr comment`, `gh pr review`, or `gh api`. That would post the same answer twice. Use `gh` to comment only where the task asks for it, such as on another issue.

## Important: Artifact and Script Requirements

**CRITICAL:** After the GitHub Action finishes running, all files modified or created are lost, and the GitHub Action runner is destroyed. Therefore:

1. **All generated code and artifacts MUST be committed** - Any files you create, modify, or generate must be committed and pushed to the repository before the action completes. Nothing will persist otherwise.

2. **Any throw-away scripts generated MUST be run immediately** - If you create temporary scripts (like `/tmp/create-issues.sh` or similar), you must execute them during the same session. They will be lost when the runner terminates.

3. **Commit and push all work** - Always end your work by committing and pushing changes to ensure they persist beyond the GitHub Action execution.
